One of the most powerful experiences I’ve had in 21 months as your Member of Congress was visiting the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency at Pearl Harbor and seeing firsthand the commitment our nation has made to identify, bring home, and reunite missing servicemembers with their families. On National POW/MIA Recognition Day, we honor the brave men and women who were held captive or who are still missing in their service to our country – including many of whom were never given a proper chance to be laid to rest. 

To this day, over 900 Marylanders who served in World War I, World War II, Korea, and Vietnam have been declared missing in action. Today and everyday, we remember the lives lost and stand with the families who never received closure for their loved ones who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. It’s why I’m committed to fighting to restore vital funding of the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency to continue its most sacred mission. If my office can be of assistance, please reach out to (410) 832-8890.

The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office finally put a price tag on the Iran war. Roughly $38 billion in the first five months alone, and another $2 to $3 billion for every month it drags on.

Even that figure doesn’t tell the whole story. 

It excludes repairs to U.S. bases damaged in the fighting and the interest on the money we're borrowing to pay for all of it. The Pentagon's own latest number to Congress is at least $42 billion.

Then Americans pay a second time, at the pump and at the checkout line. 

CBO projects the war will push inflation up half a point by early 2027, driven by energy costs. 

Diesel just hit a record national average.

Congress never authorized this war. The House has voted again and again to end it. Enough is enough.
